A word processor in Nextcloud

EditBase

EditBase is a word processor that runs inside Nextcloud and keeps every document as an ordinary HTML file in your Files. What you see on the screen is what comes out of the printer: the paper, the margins, the pictures and the rules all land where you put them, to a hundredth of a millimetre.

EditBase at a glance

Plain HTML files in your own Nextcloud, which any browser opens and prints.

What you see is what prints, to a hundredth of a millimetre.

Pages laid out like a magazine, with pictures the words run round.

Forms drawn with ruled lines on a grid of characters and lines.

Tables that calculate, with 33 functions written as in LibreOffice Calc.

An AI assistant that knows EditBase, lent by Talk-Bot.

Lay out a page like a magazine

Paste a picture and let the words run round it, take it out to the edge of the paper, or set a row of pictures with their captions underneath. A picture can stand to the left or to the right of the text, on both sides of it, above and below it, or anywhere on the page, over or under the words, in the order you choose in the Layer bar.

Paragraphs take drop caps, like the one at the top of this page, tab positions measured in millimetres and line spacing in fractions of a line, and type sizes go down to a hundredth of a point. Captions are paragraphs too, with their own style. A heading can be told to start below the pictures beside it, so that a new section never begins squeezed into a gap.

Draw forms with ruled lines

Set the page up by characters per line and lines per page, as on a manuscript sheet, and draw the ruled lines straight onto that grid. Drag a box and press Tab to add lines as you go; draw over a line to make it thin, thick, double or dotted, or erase it. The table goes into the text, so it grows as you write in it and the words below move down with it.

Characters can be spread evenly over a given width, the way a name is spread across the box of a form, and a cell can be written in from top to bottom. EditBase was checked by laying out five Japanese government forms and printing them over the original PDFs: the rules land within half a millimetre of the originals.

Plain HTML, yours to keep

Every document is saved as an HTML file in your Nextcloud, next to your other files. It opens in any browser and prints the same way without EditBase, and a search, a script or another program can read it. Nothing is locked into a format that only one program understands.

Earlier versions are kept beside the document and can be brought back at any time. A document, or a whole category, is shared with other people on the server like any other file, to read or to write, and two people can write in the same document at once, each seeing the other's typing within about a second.

Tables that calculate

A table can work like a small spreadsheet. Type a formula as you would in LibreOffice Calc, =SUM(D2:D4) or =B2*C2, and the cell shows the answer, worked out again whenever a number changes. There are 33 functions, a formula bar while you edit, and column letters and row numbers round the table.

Number format, alignment, font, borders drawn edge by edge and fill are set in tabs, as in Excel, for a whole block of cells at once. The table below is a real one: its amounts and its total are formulas, shown with a thousands separator.

Headings, contents and mathematics

Give each kind of block a style, with its typeface, size, colour, spacing, border or fill, and every paragraph of that kind follows it: this page is styled that way, not paragraph by paragraph. Choose from twenty heading designs, such as the bar at the start of the headings here, and let EditBase build a table of contents, like the one at the top of this page, and gather the footnotes at the end.

Mathematics is written as native MathML1, so a formula stays selectable text and prints sharply at any size, and formulas made in FormulaBase go into the document as they are:

x=−b±b2−4ac2a

Japanese, top to bottom

Japanese can be set from top to bottom and right to left, and on a grid of characters and lines like a manuscript sheet. Readings go over the words as ruby, emphasis dots over the characters that need them, and a highlighter over what should stand out, as in this line:

この行は、漢字(かんじ)に読(よ)み仮名(がな)を付け、大切な言葉に圏点を打ち、目立たせたい所に蛍光ペンを引いた例です。

An assistant that knows EditBase

With Talk-Bot installed, an AI assistant opens above the Pages and Layers bars. Ask it how to do something and it answers with the names of the buttons on your screen; ask it to add a heading, rewrite a paragraph or change the paper, and it makes the change as one step that Ctrl+Z takes back.

The administrator decides who may use it, whether it may search the web, and which apps it may read: other EditBase documents, RegiBase or FormulaBase. It only reads them, and RegiBase's secret fields are never shown to it.

Check, then print

“Check the document” looks over the pages before you print and finds what is wrong with them:

  1. something drawn over the edge of the paper;
  2. words hidden under a picture or a shape;
  3. a frame holding more than it can show;
  4. a photograph heavy enough to slow the file down;
  5. a page with nothing on it.

Find and replace, recorded changes, mail merge and an undo history are all built in. “Print / PDF” hands the pages to your browser exactly as they stand on the screen; its “Save as PDF” makes the finished file.
